writeup.headline: Tetra Tech rates Hold: cheap valuation and steady quality offset shrinking revenue and analyst target trims.
writeup.thesis: Tetra Tech scores 54, a Hold, because a supportive valuation is balanced by weak growth. Valuation is the strongest factor at 76. In absolute terms the multiples look moderate: P/S of 1.9x, P/FCF of 17.2x and EV/EBIT of 16.3x, with the FCF yield 0.8 pp above the 10-year Treasury yield. Against its own history the stock is cheap, with EV/EBIT cheaper than at 55 of the last 61 month-ends. Growth scores only 25, reflecting a TTM revenue decline of 7.6% and a latest-quarter revenue decline of 4.5% year on year, though growth sped up by 3.2 pp from the previous quarter. Quality (57), balance sheet (64) and trend (62) are middling to solid: there is a 10.8% FCF margin, the diluted share count is down 1.9% year on year, net debt is 1.05x FCF, and the price is 11.3% above its 200-day average. News risk (46) is slightly negative after two analyst price-target trims.
key_risks: Revenue is still shrinking, with a TTM revenue decline of 7.6%.
The business depends on government spending, so budget or contract shifts could hit results.
Analysts have been trimming targets (RBC to $44, KeyBanc to $41), and a quant service downgraded the stock to hold.
Thin gross margin of 18.8% leaves limited room if project pricing or mix worsens.
Fiscal Q4/FY2026 results on 2026-11-11 could miss the raised guidance.
